This section sets out the objects of this Act.
Climate Change Convention and Kyoto Protocol etc.
The first object of this Act is to remove greenhouse gases from the atmosphere, and avoid emissions of greenhouse gases, in order to meet Australia’s obligations under any or all of the following:
the Climate Change Convention;
the Kyoto Protocol;
the Paris Agreement;
any other international agreement.
Incentives
The second object of this Act is to create incentives for people to carry on certain offsets projects.
Carbon abatement
The third object of this Act is to increase carbon abatement in a manner that:
is consistent with the protection of Australia’s natural environment; and
improves resilience to the effects of climate change.
Purchase of carbon abatement by the Commonwealth
The fourth object of this Act is to authorise the purchase by the Commonwealth of units that represent carbon abatement.
Australia’s greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets
The fifth object of this Act is to facilitate the achievement of Australia’s greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets.
The following is a simplified outline of this Act:
• This Act sets up a scheme for the issue of Australian carbon credit units in relation to eligible offsets projects.
• Australian carbon credit units and certain other types of units may be purchased by the Commonwealth.
• An Australian carbon credit unit is personal property and is generally transferable.
• The main eligibility requirements for eligible offsets projects are as follows:
the project must be carried out in Australia;
the project must be covered by a methodology determination made under this Act.
• A methodology determination is made having regard to the offsets integrity standards set out in this Act.
• This Act is administered by the Clean Energy Regulator.

content.p: The following is a simplified outline of this Part:

section.heading: Issue of Australian carbon credit units in respect of offsets projects

content.p: Scope
This section applies if a certificate of entitlement is in force in respect of an eligible offsets project for a reporting period.
Note: For certificate of entitlement, see section 15.
Issue of units

If the project has resulted in eligible carbon abatement, the Regulator must, as soon as practicable after the day on which the certificate was issued, issue to the holder of the certificate a number of Kyoto Australian carbon credit units equal to the number specified in the certificate as the unit entitlement for that certificate.

If the project has not resulted in eligible carbon abatement, the Regulator must, as soon as practicable after the day on which the certificate was issued, issue to the holder of the certificate a number of non-Kyoto Australian carbon credit units equal to the number specified in the certificate as the unit entitlement for that certificate.
The Regulator must not issue an Australian carbon credit unit to a person in accordance with subsection (2) or (3) unless the person has a Registry account.
Note 1: See also section 49 (issue of Australian carbon credit units to registered native title bodies corporate).
Note 2: See also section 141 (issue of Australian carbon credit units in relation to projects with multiple project proponents).

The Regulator must issue an Australian carbon credit unit to a person in accordance with subsection (2) or (3) by making an entry for the unit in the person’s Registry account the account number of which is specified in the certificate.
Note 1: See also section 49 (issue of Australian carbon credit units to registered native title bodies corporate).
Note 2: See also section 141 (issue of Australian carbon credit units in relation to projects with multiple project proponents).

After the end of a reporting period for an eligible offsets project, a person may apply to the Regulator for the issue to the person of a certificate of entitlement in respect of the project for the reporting period.
Note 1: For eligible offsets project, see section 27.
Note 2: For reporting period, see section 5.
An application must:
be in writing; and
be in a form approved, in writing, by the Regulator; and
set out the account number of a Registry account of the applicant that should be specified in the certificate; and
be accompanied by such information as is specified in the regulations or the legislative rules; and
if, under the legislative rules, the application is subject to audit under this Act—be accompanied by an audit report that is:
prescribed by the legislative rules; and

under the legislative rules, a set of 2 or more applications made by the applicant is subject to audit under this Act; and

prescribed by the legislative rules; and

prescribed by the legislative rules; and

Note 2: See also section 141 (applications for certificates of entitlement in relation to projects with multiple project proponents).
The Regulator must not give a notice under paragraph (1)(eb) unless the Regulator is satisfied that it is appropriate to do so, having regard to effective risk management.
The approved form of application may provide for verification by statutory declaration of statements in applications.

The Regulator may, by written notice given to an applicant, require the applicant to give the Regulator, within the period specified in the notice, further information in connection with the application.
If the applicant breaches the requirement, the Regulator may, by written notice given to the applicant:
refuse to consider the application; or
refuse to take any action, or any further action, in relation to the application.
Scope
This section applies if an application under section 12 has been made for the issue of a certificate of entitlement in respect of an eligible offsets project for a reporting period.
Issue of certificate
If the Regulator is satisfied that:
the applicant passes the fit and proper person test; and
the applicant was, immediately before the end of the period:

part.heading: Purchase of eligible carbon credit units by the Commonwealth

content.p: • The Regulator may, on behalf of the Commonwealth, enter into contracts for the purchase by the Commonwealth of eligible carbon credit units.
• Such a contract is to be known as a carbon abatement contract.
• The Regulator may enter into a carbon abatement contract as the result of a carbon abatement purchasing process.
• The Regulator may conduct carbon abatement purchasing processes on behalf of the Commonwealth. Such processes may include reverse auctions and tender processes.
• The Regulator must have regard to certain principles and other matters when conducting a carbon abatement purchasing process.
The functions of the Regulator include entering into contracts, on behalf of the Commonwealth, for the purchase by the Commonwealth of eligible carbon credit units.
It is immaterial whether the units are in existence when the contract is entered into.
(3) For the purposes of this Act, a contract entered into under subsection (1) is to be known as a carbon abatement contract.
(4) For the purposes of this Act, if the Regulator enters into a carbon abatement contract with a person, the person is a carbon abatement contractor.

section.heading: When carbon abatement contracts may be entered into

content.p: The Regulator may enter into a carbon abatement contract under section 20B as the result of a carbon abatement purchasing process conducted by the Regulator under section 20G.
The Regulator must not enter into a carbon abatement contract under section 20B unless the carbon abatement contractor for the contract is a project proponent for an eligible offsets project.
Note: For declarations of eligible offsets projects, see section 27. The requirements for such a declaration include that the project proponent for the project passes the fit and proper person test.
The Regulator must not enter into a carbon abatement contract under section 20B (otherwise than by way of novation) if any of the eligible carbon credit units to be purchased under the contract:
were issued; or
at the time of purchase, would have been issued;
in respect of an eligible offsets project of a kind specified in the legislative rules.
In setting the duration of a proposed carbon abatement contract, the Regulator must have regard to the following matters:
such matters as are specified in the legislative rules;
such other matters (if any) as the Regulator considers relevant.
In exercising the power to make legislative rules for the purposes of paragraph (1)(a), the Minister must have regard to the following matters:
the principle that, in general, the duration of a carbon abatement contract for the purchase of Australian carbon credit units should not be longer than 7 years;

the principle that a longer duration of a carbon abatement contract for the purchase of Australian carbon credit units may be appropriate if the units are, or are to be, derived from an eligible offsets project that has a crediting period of more than 7 years;
such other matters (if any) as the Minister considers relevant.

section.heading: Regulator has powers etc. of the Commonwealth

content.p: The Regulator, on behalf of the Commonwealth, has all the rights, responsibilities, duties and powers of the Commonwealth in relation to the Commonwealth’s capacity as a party to a carbon abatement contract.
Without limiting subsection (1):
an amount payable by the Commonwealth under a carbon abatement contract is to be paid by the Regulator on behalf of the Commonwealth; and
an amount payable to the Commonwealth under a carbon abatement contract is to be paid to the Regulator on behalf of the Commonwealth; and
the Regulator may institute an action or proceeding on behalf of the Commonwealth in relation to a matter that concerns a carbon abatement contract.

section.heading: Conferral of powers on the Regulator

content.p: The Regulator may exercise a power conferred on the Regulator by a carbon abatement contract.
For the purposes of this Act, a carbon abatement purchasing process means any of the following processes:
a reverse auction;
a tender process;
any other process;
for the purchase by the Commonwealth of eligible carbon credit units. (It is immaterial whether the units are in existence when the process is conducted.)

section.heading: Conduct of carbon abatement purchasing processes

content.p: The Regulator may, on behalf of the Commonwealth, conduct one or more carbon abatement purchasing processes.
In exercising the power conferred by subsection (1), the Regulator must have regard to:
the principles set out in subsection (3); and
such other matters (if any) as are specified in the legislative rules.

Without limiting paragraph (2)(b), the legislative rules may provide that the Regulator must exclude from one or more carbon abatement purchasing processes carbon abatement that results, or is to result, from the carrying out of an offsets project of a specified kind.
Principles for conduct of carbon abatement purchasing processes
The principles for conducting a carbon abatement purchasing process are that the process should:
facilitate the Commonwealth purchasing carbon abatement at the least cost; and
maximise the amount of carbon abatement that the Commonwealth can purchase; and
be conducted in a manner that ensures that administrative costs are reasonable; and
be conducted in a manner that ensures the integrity of the process; and
encourage competition; and
provide for fair and ethical treatment of all participants in the process.
To avoid doubt, the mere fact that a person is a project proponent for an eligible offsets project does not automatically entitle the person to participate in a carbon abatement purchasing process.

section.heading: Legislative rules may provide for certain matters relating to purchased eligible carbon credit units etc.

content.p: The legislative rules may make provision for and in relation to any or all of the following matters in respect of eligible carbon credit units purchased by the Commonwealth under carbon abatement contracts:
transferring purchased units to or from a specified Commonwealth Registry account;
selling units held in such an account;
prohibiting or restricting the transfer of units from such an account;
cancelling units for which there are entries in such an account.
Note: For designation of Commonwealth Registry accounts, see section 12 of the Australian National Registry of Emissions Units Act 2011.
Restoration of units that were transferred by mistake
If:

one or more eligible carbon credit units were transferred from a Registry account kept by a person to a Commonwealth Registry account specified in legislative rules made for the purposes of paragraph (1)(a); and
the units have been cancelled; and
the Regulator is satisfied that the units were transferred by mistake;
then:
(d) the Regulator must, by written notice given to the person, determine that the units that were transferred are restored units for the purposes of this section; and
a restored unit is taken never to have been cancelled; and
the Regulator must make an entry for a restored unit in a Registry account kept by the person.
Subsection (2) does not affect the validity of the removal of the entry of a restored unit from the Commonwealth Registry account.
A determination made under paragraph (2)(d) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Certain instruments relating to Commonwealth procurement are not applicable

content.p: An instrument made under section 105B of the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013 does not apply in relation to the functions and powers of the Regulator under section 20B or 20G of this Act.
Note: Section 105B of the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013 provides for the making of instruments relating to procurement.

section.heading: Carbon abatement contracts are not instruments made under this Act

content.p: To avoid doubt, a carbon abatement contract is taken not to be an instrument made under this Act.
The following is a simplified outline of this Part:
• The Regulator may declare an offsets project to be an eligible offsets project.
• The Regulator may vary or revoke a declaration of an eligible offsets project.

section.heading: Application for declaration of eligible offsets project

content.p: A person may apply to the Regulator for the declaration of an offsets project as an eligible offsets project.
Note: The Regulator has a function of providing advice and assistance in relation to the making of applications: see section 286.
An application must:
be in writing; and
be in a form approved, in writing, by the Regulator; and
be accompanied by such information as is specified in the regulations or the legislative rules; and

if the project is of a kind specified in the regulations or the legislative rules—be accompanied by a prescribed audit report prepared by a registered greenhouse and energy auditor who has been appointed as an audit team leader for the purpose; and
if an indigenous land use agreement is relevant to the Regulator’s decision on the application—be accompanied by a copy of the agreement; and
if the project is a sequestration offsets project—include either:
a request that the project be treated as a 100-year permanence period project; or
a request that the project be treated as a 25-year permanence period project; and
if:
the project is an area-based offsets project; and
the project area, or any of the project areas, for the project is covered by a regional natural resource management plan;
be accompanied by a statement about whether the project is consistent with the plan; and
be accompanied by such other documents (if any) as are specified in the regulations or the legislative rules; and
be accompanied by the fee (if any) specified in the regulations or the legislative rules.
Note: For specification by class, see subsection 13(3) of the Legislation Act 2003.
The approved form of application may provide for verification by statutory declaration of statements in applications.
A fee specified under paragraph (1)(i) must not be such as to amount to taxation.
(5) Paragraph (1)(d) of this section does not, by implication, affect the application of subsection 13(3) of the Legislation Act 2003 to:
another paragraph of subsection (1) of this section; or
another instrument under this Act.

The Regulator may, by written notice given to an applicant, require the applicant to give the Regulator, within the period specified in the notice, further information in connection with the application.
If the applicant breaches the requirement, the Regulator may, by written notice given to the applicant:
refuse to consider the application; or
refuse to take any action, or any further action, in relation to the application.
An applicant may withdraw the application at any time before the Regulator makes a decision on the application.
This Act does not prevent the applicant from making a fresh application.
If:
the applicant withdraws the application; and
the applicant has paid a fee in relation to the application;
the Regulator must, on behalf of the Commonwealth, refund the application fee.
Scope
This section applies if:
an application under section 22 has been made, or purportedly made, for a declaration of an offsets project as an eligible offsets project; and
the Regulator is satisfied that the application relates to 2 or more offsets projects.
Application may be split

The Regulator may, by written notice given to the applicant, determine that this Act has effect as if the applicant had made a separate application under section 22 in relation to each of the offsets projects referred to in paragraph (1)(b) of this section.
Scope
This section applies if an application under section 22 has been made for a declaration of an offsets project as an eligible offsets project.
Declaration
(2) After considering the application, the Regulator may, by writing, declare that the offsets project is an eligible offsets project for the purposes of this Act.
A declaration under subsection (2) must:
identify the name of the project; and
if the project is an area-based offsets project—identify, in accordance with the regulations or the legislative rules, the project area or project areas; and
identify the project proponent for the project; and
identify the applicable methodology determination for the project; and
identify the crediting period or periods for the project; and
identify such attributes of the project as are specified in the regulations or the legislative rules; and
if:
the project is a sequestration offsets project; and
the application included a request that the project be treated as a 100-year permanence period project;
declare that the project is a 100-year permanence period project; and
if:
the project is a sequestration offsets project; and
the application included a request that the project be treated as a 25-year permanence period project;
declare that the project is a 25-year permanence period project.
Criteria for declaration
The Regulator must not declare that the offsets project is an eligible offsets project unless the Regulator is satisfied that:
the project is, or is to be, carried on in Australia; and
the project is covered by a methodology determination; and
the project meets such requirements as are set out in the methodology determination in accordance with paragraph 106(1)(b); and
the project meets the additionality requirements set out in subsection (4A) of this section; and
the applicant is the project proponent for the project; and
the applicant passes the fit and proper person test; and
if the project is a sequestration offsets project—the project area, or each project area, meets the requirements set out in subsection (5) of this section; and
the project meets the eligibility requirements (if any) specified in the regulations or the legislative rules; and
the project is not an excluded offsets project.
Note 1: Methodology determinations are made under section 106.
Note 2: For the fit and proper person test, see section 60.
Note 3: For excluded offsets project, see section 56.
The additionality requirements mentioned in paragraph (4)(d) are:
either:
(i) the requirement (the newness requirement) that the project has not begun to be implemented; or

if the methodology determination that covers the project specifies, for the purposes of this subparagraph, one or more requirements that are expressed to be in lieu of the newness requirement—those requirements; and
either:
(i) the requirement (the regulatory additionality requirement) that the project is not required to be carried out by or under a law of the Commonwealth, a State or a Territory; or

if the methodology determination that covers the project specifies, for the purposes of this subparagraph, one or more requirements that are expressed to be in lieu of the regulatory additionality requirement—those requirements; and
either:

(i) the requirement (the government program requirement) that the project would be unlikely to be carried out under another Commonwealth, State or Territory government program or scheme in the absence of a declaration of the project as an eligible offsets project; or
if the legislative rules specify, for the purposes of this subparagraph, one or more requirements that are expressed to be in lieu of the government program requirement—those requirements.

For the purposes of subparagraph (4A)(a)(i), in determining whether the project has begun to be implemented, disregard any of the following activities that have been, or are being, undertaken in relation to the project:
conducting a feasibility study for the project;
planning or designing the project;
obtaining regulatory approvals for the project;
obtaining consents relating to the project;
obtaining advice relating to the project;
conducting negotiations relating to the project;
sampling to establish a baseline for the project;
an activity specified in the legislative rules;
an activity that is ancillary or incidental to any of the above activities.
For the purposes of subparagraph (4A)(a)(i), the following are examples of when a project has begun to be implemented:
making a final investment decision in relation to the project;
acquiring or leasing a tangible asset (other than land) that is for use wholly or mainly for the purposes of the project;
commencing construction work for the purposes of the project;
in the case of a sequestration offsets project—preparing soil for seeding or planting that is for the purposes of the project;
in the case of a sequestration offsets project—seeding, planting or fertilising plants that are for the purposes of the project;
in the case of a sequestration offsets project—installing an irrigation or drainage system for the purposes of the project.
(4D) For the purposes of paragraph (4C)(a), final investment decision has the meaning generally accepted within the corporate finance community.
For the purposes of paragraph (4C)(b), disregard an asset that is a minor asset.
The requirements mentioned in paragraph (4)(g) are:
the project area is Torrens system land or Crown land; and
the project area is not specified in the regulations or the legislative rules.
Note: For specification by class, see subsection 13(3) of the Legislation Act 2003.
The Regulator must not make a declaration under subsection (2) if:
the project is an area-based offsets project; and
the project area is, or any of the project areas are, to any extent subject to a carbon maintenance obligation.
(11) The Regulator must not make a declaration under subsection (2) in relation to a project (the new project) if:
(a) a notice was given under section 88, 89, 90 or 91 in relation to a project (the prior project) that is or was:
an eligible offsets project; and
a sequestration offsets project; and
the new project is an area-based offsets project; and
the project area, or any of the project areas, for the new project was or were identified in the relevant section 27 declaration as the project area or project areas for the prior project; and
the notice required a person to relinquish a particular number of Australian carbon credit units; and
the person did not comply with the requirement within 90 days after the notice was given; and

the penalty payable under section 179 in respect of the non-compliance with the requirement (including any late payment penalty payable under section 180 in relation to the section 179 penalty) has not been paid in full.
Timing
The Regulator must take all reasonable steps to ensure that a decision is made on the application:
if the Regulator requires the applicant to give further information under subsection 24(1) in relation to the application—within 90 days after the applicant gave the Regulator the information; or
otherwise—within 90 days after the application was made.
When a declaration takes effect
A declaration under subsection (2) takes effect when it is made.
Notification of declaration
As soon as practicable after making a declaration under subsection (2), the Regulator must give a copy of the declaration to:
the applicant; and
if the declaration relates to a sequestration offsets project—the relevant land registration official.
Refusal
If the Regulator decides to refuse to declare the offsets project as an eligible offsets project, the Regulator must give written notice of the decision to the applicant.
Declaration is not legislative instrument
A declaration made under subsection (2) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Suspension of processing of applications for declarations of eligible offsets projects

content.p: Order
The Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee may, by legislative instrument, order that, if:
an application is made under section 22 during a specified period; and
the application relates to an offsets project that is covered by a specified methodology determination;
the Regulator must not:
consider the application during that period; or
make a decision on the application during that period.
A period specified in an order under subsection (1):
must start at the commencement of the order; and
must not be longer than 12 months.

The Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee must not make an order under subsection (1) that relates to a methodology determination unless the Committee is satisfied that there is reasonable evidence that the methodology determination does not comply with one or more of the offsets integrity standards.
Before making an order under subsection (1), the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee must inform the Minister of the Committee’s proposal to make the order.
Compliance with order
The Regulator must comply with an order under subsection (1).
Timing of decision on application
If an application made under section 22 is or was covered by an order under subsection (1) of this section, subsection 27(14) does not apply to the application.
Note: Subsection 27(14) deals with the timing of decisions on applications.

section.heading: Declaration may be subject to condition about obtaining regulatory approvals

content.p: Scope
This section applies if:
an application under section 22 has been made for a declaration of an offsets project as an eligible offsets project; and
the Regulator makes a declaration under section 27 in relation to the project; and
the Regulator is not satisfied that all regulatory approvals have been obtained for the project.
Condition

The Regulator must specify in the declaration that the declaration is subject to the condition that all regulatory approvals must be obtained for the project before the end of the first reporting period for the project.

section.heading: Declaration may be subject to condition about obtaining consents from eligible interest holders

content.p: Scope
This section applies if:
an application under section 22 has been made for a declaration of an offsets project as an eligible offsets project; and
the Regulator makes a declaration under section 27 in relation to the project; and
(c) the Regulator is satisfied that there are one or more persons (the relevant interest-holders) who:
hold an eligible interest in the project area, or any of the project areas, for the project; and
have not consented, in writing, to the making of the application.
Condition

The Regulator must specify in the declaration that the declaration is subject to the condition that the written consent of each relevant interest-holder to the existence of the declaration must be obtained before the end of the first reporting period for the project.
Consents
A consent mentioned in subparagraph (1)(c)(ii) or subsection (2) must be in a form approved, in writing, by the Regulator.
A consent mentioned in subparagraph (1)(c)(ii) or subsection (2) may be set out in a registered indigenous land use agreement.
Subsection (3) does not apply to a consent mentioned in subparagraph (1)(c)(ii) or subsection (2) if the consent is set out in a registered indigenous land use agreement.
Registered indigenous land use agreements
If:
the declaration is in force; and
a consent mentioned in subparagraph (1)(c)(ii) or subsection (2) of this section was set out in a registered indigenous land use agreement;

details of the agreement must not be removed from the Register of Indigenous Land Use Agreements under subparagraph 199C(1)(c)(ii) of the Native Title Act 1993 without the written consent of the Regulator.

division.heading: Variation of declaration of eligible offsets project

section.heading: Voluntary variation of declaration of eligible offsets project in relation to the project area or project areas

content.p: Regulations or legislative rules

The regulations or the legislative rules may make provision for and in relation to empowering the Regulator to vary a declaration under section 27 in relation to an area-based offsets project so far as the declaration identifies the project area or project areas.

Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must not empower the Regulator to vary a declaration unless the project proponent for the project applies to the Regulator for the variation of the declaration.
Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) may make provision for or in relation to any or all of the following matters:
applications for variations under those regulations or legislative rules, as the case may be;
the approval by the Regulator of a form for such an application;
information that must accompany such an application;
documents that must accompany such an application;
verification by statutory declaration of statements in such an application;
consents that must be obtained for the making of such an application;
authorising a person to issue a certificate in relation to such an application;
the fee (if any) that must accompany such an application;
the withdrawal of such an application;
empowering the Regulator:
to require an applicant to give the Regulator further information in connection with such an application; and
if the applicant breaches the requirement—to refuse to consider the application, or to refuse to take any action, or any further action, in relation to the application.
Subsection (3) does not limit subsection (1).
A fee mentioned in paragraph (3)(i) must not be such as to amount to taxation.

Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must provide that, if a declaration of an eligible offsets project is varied in accordance with those regulations or legislative rules, as the case may be, the Regulator must give a copy of the variation to:
the applicant for the variation; and
if the declaration relates to a sequestration offsets project—the relevant land registration official.

Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must provide that, if the Regulator decides to refuse to vary a declaration of an eligible offsets project in accordance with an application for variation under those regulations or legislative rules, as the case may be, the Regulator must give written notice of the decision to the applicant for the variation.
Registered indigenous land use agreements
If:
a declaration of an eligible offsets project is varied in accordance with regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1); and
a consent to the making of the application for the variation was set out in a registered indigenous land use agreement;

details of the agreement must not be removed from the Register of Indigenous Land Use Agreements under subparagraph 199C(1)(c)(ii) of the Native Title Act 1993 without the written consent of the Regulator.
References to eligible offsets project

If a declaration of an eligible offsets project is varied in accordance with regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1), a reference in this Act, the regulations or the legislative rules to the eligible offsets project is a reference to the eligible offsets project as varied.

section.heading: Voluntary variation of declaration of eligible offsets project in relation to the project proponent

content.p: Regulations or legislative rules

The regulations or the legislative rules may make provision for and in relation to empowering the Regulator to vary a declaration under section 27 in relation to an offsets project so far as the declaration identifies the project proponent for the project.

Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must not empower the Regulator to vary a declaration unless the project proponent for the project applies to the Regulator for the variation of the declaration.
Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) may make provision for or in relation to any or all of the following matters:
applications for variations under those regulations or legislative rules, as the case may be;
the approval by the Regulator of a form for such an application;
information that must accompany such an application;
documents that must accompany such an application;
verification by statutory declaration of statements in such an application;
the fee (if any) that must accompany such an application;
the withdrawal of such an application;
empowering the Regulator:
to require an applicant to give the Regulator further information in connection with such an application; and
if the applicant breaches the requirement—to refuse to consider the application, or to refuse to take any action, or any further action, in relation to the application;

empowering the Regulator to require the applicant to give security to the Commonwealth in relation to the fulfilment by the applicant of any requirements to relinquish Australian carbon credit units that may be imposed on the applicant under this Part in relation to the project.
Subsection (3) does not limit subsection (1).
A fee mentioned in paragraph (3)(f) must not be such as to amount to taxation.

Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must provide that, if a declaration of an eligible offsets project is varied in accordance with those regulations or legislative rules, as the case may be, the Regulator must give a copy of the variation to:
the applicant for the variation; and
if the declaration relates to a sequestration offsets project—the relevant land registration official.

Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must provide that, if a declaration of an eligible offsets project is varied in accordance with those regulations or legislative rules, as the case may be, the variation takes effect:
when it is made; or
if:
the Regulator makes a written determination specifying an earlier day; and
the applicant for the variation has consented to the determination of the earlier day;
on the day so determined.
A determination made under subparagraph (7)(b)(i) is not a legislative instrument.

Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must provide that, if the Regulator decides to refuse to vary a declaration of an eligible offsets project in accordance with an application for variation under those regulations or legislative rules, as the case may be, the Regulator must give written notice of the decision to the applicant for the variation.
References to eligible offsets project

If a declaration of an eligible offsets project is varied in accordance with regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1), a reference in this Act, the regulations or the legislative rules to the eligible offsets project is a reference to the eligible offsets project as varied.

section.heading: Voluntary variation of conditional declaration of eligible offsets project—condition of declaration has been met

content.p: Scope
This section applies to a declaration under section 27 in relation to an offsets project if the declaration is subject to a condition mentioned in subsection 28(2) or 28A(2).
Regulations or legislative rules
The regulations or the legislative rules may make provision for and in relation to empowering the Regulator to vary such a declaration by removing such a condition.
Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (2) must not empower the Regulator to vary a declaration unless:
the project proponent for the project applies to the Regulator for the variation of the declaration; and
the Regulator is satisfied that the condition has been met.
Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (2) may make provision for or in relation to any or all of the following matters:
applications for variations under those regulations or legislative rules, as the case may be;
the approval by the Regulator of a form for such an application;
information that must accompany such an application;
documents that must accompany such an application;
verification by statutory declaration of statements in such an application;
the fee (if any) that must accompany such an application;
the withdrawal of such an application;
empowering the Regulator:
to require an applicant to give the Regulator further information in connection with such an application; and
if the applicant breaches the requirement—to refuse to consider the application, or to refuse to take any action, or any further action, in relation to the application.

A fee mentioned in paragraph (4)(f) must not be such as to amount to taxation.

Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (2) must provide that, if a declaration of an eligible offsets project is varied in accordance with those regulations or legislative rules, as the case may be, the Regulator must give a copy of the variation to:
the applicant for the variation; and
if the declaration relates to a sequestration offsets project—the relevant land registration official.

Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (2) must provide that, if the Regulator decides to refuse to vary a declaration of an eligible offsets project in accordance with an application for variation under those regulations or legislative rules, as the case may be, the Regulator must give written notice of the decision to the applicant for the variation.
References to eligible offsets project

If a declaration of an eligible offsets project is varied in accordance with regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (2), a reference in this Act, the regulations or the legislative rules to the eligible offsets project is a reference to the eligible offsets project as varied.

section.heading: No variation of declaration of eligible offsets project as a 100-year or 25-year permanence period project

content.p: Scope
This section applies to a declaration under section 27 in relation to an offsets project if the declaration:
declares that the project is a 100-year permanence period project; or
declares that the project is a 25-year permanence period project.
Regulator must not vary permanence period
The Regulator must not:
if paragraph (1)(a) applies—vary the declaration to declare that the project is a 25-year permanence period project; or
if paragraph (1)(b) applies—vary the declaration to declare that the project is a 100-year permanence period project.

division.heading: Revocation of declaration of eligible offsets project

content.p: Subdivision A—Voluntary revocation of declaration of eligible offsets project

section.heading: Voluntary revocation of declaration of eligible offsets project—units issued

content.p: The regulations or the legislative rules may make provision for and in relation to empowering the Regulator to revoke a declaration under section 27 in relation to an offsets project.
Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must not empower the Regulator to revoke a declaration unless:
one or more Australian carbon credit units have been issued in relation to the project in accordance with Part 2; and
the project proponent for the project applies to the Regulator for the revocation of the declaration; and
if the project is a sequestration offsets project:
before the application was made, the applicant voluntarily relinquished a number of Australian carbon credit units in order to satisfy a condition for the revocation of the declaration; and
the number of relinquished units equals the net total number of Australian carbon credit units issued in relation to the project in accordance with Part 2.
Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) may make provision for or in relation to either or both of the following matters:
applications for revocations under those regulations or legislative rules, as the case may be;
the approval by the Regulator of a form for such an application.
Subsection (3) does not limit subsection (1).

Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must provide that, if a declaration of an eligible offsets project is revoked in accordance with those regulations or legislative rules, as the case may be, the Regulator must give a copy of the revocation to:
the applicant for the revocation; and
if the declaration relates to a sequestration offsets project—the relevant land registration official.

section.heading: Voluntary revocation of declaration of eligible offsets project—no units issued

content.p: The regulations or the legislative rules may make provision for and in relation to empowering the Regulator to revoke a declaration under section 27 in relation to an offsets project.
Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must not empower the Regulator to revoke a declaration unless:
no Australian carbon credit units have been issued in relation to the project in accordance with Part 2; and
the project proponent for the project applies to the Regulator for the revocation of the declaration.
Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) may make provision for or in relation to either or both of the following matters:
applications for revocations under those regulations or legislative rules, as the case may be;
the approval by the Regulator of a form for such an application.
Subsection (3) does not limit subsection (1).

Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must provide that, if a declaration of an eligible offsets project is revoked in accordance with those regulations or legislative rules, as the case may be, the Regulator must give a copy of the revocation to:
the applicant for the revocation; and
if the declaration relates to a sequestration offsets project—the relevant land registration official.
Subdivision B—Unilateral revocation of declaration of eligible offsets project

section.heading: Unilateral revocation of declaration of eligible offsets project—condition of declaration has not been met

content.p: The regulations or the legislative rules may make provision for and in relation to empowering the Regulator to revoke a declaration under section 27 in relation to an offsets project.
Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must not empower the Regulator to revoke a declaration unless:
the declaration is subject to a condition mentioned in subsection 28(2) or 28A(2); and
the Regulator is satisfied that the condition has not been met.
Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must require the Regulator to consult the project proponent for the project before deciding to revoke a declaration.

the project proponent; and
if the declaration relates to a sequestration offsets project—the relevant land registration official.

section.heading: Unilateral revocation of declaration of eligible offsets project—eligibility requirements not met etc.

content.p: The regulations or the legislative rules may make provision for and in relation to empowering the Regulator to revoke a declaration under section 27 in relation to an offsets project.

Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must not empower the Regulator to revoke a declaration unless the Regulator is satisfied that the project does not meet a requirement that is:
set out in subsection 27(4); and
specified in regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of this paragraph.
Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must require the Regulator to consult the project proponent for the project before deciding to revoke a declaration.

Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must provide that, if a declaration of an eligible offsets project is revoked in accordance with those regulations or legislative rules, as the case may be, the Regulator must give a copy of the revocation to:
the project proponent; and
if the declaration relates to a sequestration offsets project—the relevant land registration official.

section.heading: Unilateral revocation of declaration of eligible offsets project—project proponent ceases to pass the fit and proper person test

content.p: The regulations or the legislative rules may make provision for and in relation to empowering the Regulator to revoke a declaration under section 27 in relation to an offsets project.
Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must not empower the Regulator to revoke a declaration unless:
the project proponent for the project ceases to pass the fit and proper person test; and

the project proponent; and
if the declaration relates to a sequestration offsets project—the relevant land registration official.

section.heading: Unilateral revocation of declaration of eligible offsets project—person responsible for carrying out project ceases to be the project proponent

content.p: The regulations or the legislative rules may make provision for and in relation to empowering the Regulator to revoke a declaration under section 27 in relation to an offsets project.

the person who is responsible for carrying out the project ceases to be the project proponent for the project; and
90 days pass after the cessation, and the person who, at the end of that 90-day period, is responsible for carrying out the project is not:
the project proponent for the project; and
a person who passes the fit and proper person test.
Note: For the fit and proper person test, see section 60.
Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must require the Regulator to consult the project proponent for the project before deciding to revoke a declaration.

Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must provide that, if a declaration of an eligible offsets project is revoked in accordance with those regulations or legislative rules, as the case may be, the Regulator must give a copy of the revocation to:
the person who is responsible for carrying out the project; and
if the declaration relates to a sequestration offsets project—the relevant land registration official.

section.heading: Unilateral revocation of declaration of eligible offsets project—false or misleading information

content.p: The regulations or the legislative rules may make provision for and in relation to empowering the Regulator to revoke a declaration under section 27 in relation to an offsets project.
Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must not empower the Regulator to revoke a declaration unless:
information was given by a person to the Regulator in connection with the project; and
the information was:
contained in an application under this Act, the regulations or the legislative rules; or
given in connection with an application under this Act, the regulations or the legislative rules; or
contained in an offsets report; or
contained in a notification under Part 6; and
the information was false or misleading in a material particular.
Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must require the Regulator to consult the project proponent for the project before deciding to revoke a declaration.

Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must provide that, if a declaration of an eligible offsets project is revoked in accordance with those regulations or legislative rules, as the case may be, the Regulator must give a copy of the revocation to:
the project proponent; and

A notice under subparagraph (4)(b)(ii) may be included in the offsets report for the project given under subsection 76(1).

Scope
This section applies to an eligible offsets project if:
the project was an eligible offsets project immediately before the commencement of this Part; and
(b) the project is not covered by the Carbon Credits (Carbon Farming Initiative) (Avoided Deforestation) Methodology Determination 2013.
Project has 2 crediting periods
If the project is a sequestration offsets project, then, for the purposes of this Act, the project has 2 crediting periods, as follows:
the first crediting period for the project is the period:
beginning when the declaration of the project under section 27 took effect; and
ending immediately before the commencement of this Part;
the second crediting period for the project is:
the period of 25 years; or
if another period is specified in the applicable methodology determination for the project—that other period;
that began at the commencement of this Part.
If:
the project is an emissions avoidance offsets project; and
the project is not a designated savanna project;
then, for the purposes of this Act, the project has 2 crediting periods, as follows:
the first crediting period for the project is the period:
beginning when the declaration of the project under section 27 took effect; and
ending immediately before the commencement of this Part;
the second crediting period for the project is:
the period of 7 years; or
if another period is specified in the applicable methodology determination for the project—that other period;
that began at the commencement of this Part.
If:
the project is an emissions avoidance offsets project; and
the project is a designated savanna project;
then, for the purposes of this Act, the project has 2 crediting periods, as follows:
the first crediting period for the project is the period:
beginning when the declaration of the project under section 27 took effect; and
ending immediately before 1 January next following the commencement of this Part;
the second crediting period for the project is:
the period of 25 years; or
if another period is specified in the applicable methodology determination for the project—that other period;
that began at the start of 1 January next following the commencement of this Part.

The project cannot have more than 2 crediting periods.

section.heading: Crediting period—transitional rule for avoided deforestation projects

content.p: Scope
This section applies to an eligible offsets project if:
either:
the project was an eligible offsets project immediately before the commencement of this Part; or

(ii) the project became an eligible offsets project after the commencement of this Part as the result of an ERF transitional application (within the meaning of Division 2 of Part 2 of Schedule 1 to the Carbon Farming Initiative Amendment Act 2014); and
(b) the project is covered by the Carbon Credits (Carbon Farming Initiative) (Avoided Deforestation) Methodology Determination 2013.
Crediting period
Despite any other provision of this Part, the crediting period for the project is:
the first crediting period for the project worked out under section 69 as it stood immediately before the commencement of this Part; or
if another period is specified in the applicable methodology determination for the project—that other period that began when the declaration of the project under section 27 took effect.
No subsequent crediting periods
The project cannot have more than one crediting period.
The following is a simplified outline of this Part:
• The project proponent for an eligible offsets project must give the Regulator an offsets report for a period that is expressed to be a reporting period for the project.
• The first reporting period must begin at the start of the crediting period for the project.
• Each subsequent reporting period must begin immediately after the end of the previous reporting period.
• A reporting period for a sequestration offsets project must not be:
shorter than 6 months (or such lesser number of months as is specified in the legislative rules); or
longer than 5 years.
• A reporting period for an emissions avoidance offsets project must not be:
shorter than 6 months (or such lesser number of months as is specified in the legislative rules); or
longer than 2 years.
• The Regulator must be notified of certain events relating to eligible offsets projects.
Report for first reporting period
The project proponent for an eligible offsets project must, in accordance with this section, give the Regulator a written report about the project for a period that:
is expressed to be a reporting period for the project; and
begins:

if the project has 2 crediting periods—at the start of the first crediting period; and
is not shorter than:
6 months; or
if, under the legislative rules, a specified lesser number of months is the minimum number of months applicable to the report—that specified lesser number of months; and
if the project is a sequestration offsets project—is not longer than 5 years; and
if the project is an emissions avoidance offsets project—is not longer than 2 years.

Note: Under section 15, the general rule is that the Regulator may only issue a certificate of entitlement to Australian carbon credit units in relation to a reporting period for an eligible offsets project if the reporting period is included in a crediting period for the project.
Reports for subsequent reporting periods
The project proponent for an eligible offsets project must, in accordance with this section, give the Regulator a written report about the project for a period that:
is expressed to be a reporting period for the project; and
begins immediately after the end of the previous reporting period for the project; and
is not shorter than:
6 months; or
if, under the legislative rules, a specified lesser number of months is the minimum number of months applicable to the report—that specified lesser number of months; and
if the project is a sequestration offsets project—is not longer than 5 years; and
if the project is an emissions avoidance offsets project—is not longer than 2 years; and
if the project is an emissions avoidance offsets project—is included in:
a crediting period for the project; or
the extended accounting period (if any) for the project.

Note 1: Under section 15, the general rule is that the Regulator may only issue a certificate of entitlement to Australian carbon credit units in relation to a reporting period for an eligible offsets project if the reporting period is included in a crediting period for the project.
Note 2: See also section 77.
Offsets report
(3) A report under this section is to be known as an offsets report.

The Regulator must not give a notice under paragraph (4)(cb) unless the Regulator is satisfied that it is appropriate to do so, having regard to effective risk management.

If, under the applicable methodology determination, the project proponent for the project is subject to a requirement to include specified information relating to the project in the offsets report, the offsets report must include that information.

section.heading: Declaration that offsets report requirement does not apply

content.p: Regulations or legislative rules
The regulations or the legislative rules may make provision for and in relation to empowering the Regulator to declare that subsection 76(2) does not apply to a particular eligible offsets project.
Regulations or legislative rules made for the purposes of subsection (1) must not empower the Regulator to make a declaration unless:

part.heading: Requirements to relinquish Australian carbon credit units

content.p: The following is a simplified outline of this Part:
• Australian carbon credit units may be required to be relinquished if:
the issue of the units is attributable to the giving of false or misleading information; or
the units were issued in relation to a sequestration offsets project, and the declaration of the sequestration offsets project as an eligible offsets project has been revoked; or
the units were issued in relation to a sequestration offsets project, and there has been a complete or partial reversal of sequestration.
For the purposes of this Act, the permanence period for an eligible offsets project is:
if the project is a 100-year permanence period project—the 100-year permanence period for the project; or
if the project is a 25-year permanence period project—25 years.
(1) For the purposes of this Act, the 100-year permanence period for an eligible offsets project is:
100 years; or

if, at the time when the declaration of the project as an eligible offsets project was made, a greater number of years was specified in the regulations or the legislative rules—that greater number of years.
However, if:
the regulations or the legislative rules specify a number of years that is less than 100 years; and
those regulations or legislative rules, as the case may be, are made after the time when the declaration of a project as an eligible offsets project was made;
then, despite subsection (1), that lesser number of years is the 100-year permanence period for the eligible offsets project.

section.heading: Requirement to relinquish—false or misleading information

content.p: Scope
This section applies if:
a number of Australian carbon credit units have been issued to a person in relation to an eligible offsets project; and
information was given by the person to the Regulator in connection with the project; and
the information was:
contained in an application under this Act, the regulations or the legislative rules; or
given in connection with an application under this Act, the regulations or the legislative rules; or
contained in an offsets report; or
contained in a notification under Part 6; and
the information was false or misleading in a material particular; and
the issue of any or all of the units was directly or indirectly attributable to the false or misleading information.
Relinquishment
The Regulator may, by written notice given to the person, require the person to relinquish a specified number of Australian carbon credit units.
The specified number must not exceed the number of Australian carbon credit units the issue of which was directly or indirectly attributable to the false or misleading information.
The person must comply with the requirement within 90 days after the notice was given.
