holds or performs the duties of an Executive Level 2 position, or an equivalent position, in the Department.

The Minister must ensure that at least one of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee members is an officer of the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation nominated by the Chief Executive of the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation.
The Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee holds office on a full-time basis.
An Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member (other than the Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee) holds office on a part-time basis.

section.heading: Period for appointment for Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee members

content.p: An Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member holds office for the period specified in the instrument of appointment. The period must not exceed 5 years.
Note: For re-appointment, see the Acts Interpretation Act 1901.

section.heading: Acting Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee members

content.p: Acting Chair of Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee
The Minister may appoint an Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member to act as the Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee:
during a vacancy in the office of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee Chair (whether or not an appointment has previously been made to the office); or
during any period, or during all periods, when the Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee:
is absent from duty or from Australia; or
is, for any reason, unable to perform the duties of the office.
Acting Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member (other than the Chair)
The Minister may appoint a person to act as an Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member (other than the Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee):

during a vacancy in the office of an Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member (other than the Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee), whether or not an appointment has previously been made to the office; or
during any period, or during all periods, when an Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member (other than the Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee):
is absent from duty or Australia; or
is, for any reason, unable to perform the duties of the office.
Eligibility
A person is not eligible for appointment to act as:
the Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee; or
an Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member (other than the Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee);
unless the person is eligible for appointment as an Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member.
Note 1: See subsection 257(2).
Note 2: For rules that apply to acting appointments, see sections 33AB and 33A of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901.

The regulations or the legislative rules may prescribe the procedures to be followed at or in relation to meetings of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee, including matters relating to the following:
the convening of meetings of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee;
the number of Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee members who are to constitute a quorum;

the selection of an Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member to preside at meetings of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee in the absence of the Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee;
the manner in which questions arising at a meeting of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee are to be decided.
A resolution is taken to have been passed at a meeting of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee if:

without meeting, a majority of Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee members indicate agreement with the resolution in accordance with the method determined by the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee under subsection (3); and

all Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee members were informed of the proposed resolution, or reasonable efforts had been made to inform all Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee members of the proposed resolution.
Subsection (2) applies only if the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee:
determines that it applies; and
determines the method by which Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee members are to indicate agreement with resolutions.
If an Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member is an APS employee in the Department, the member:
is not entitled to vote for a resolution at a meeting of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee; and
is not entitled to indicate agreement with a resolution as mentioned in paragraph (2)(a); and
is not to be counted for the purposes of determining whether a majority of Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee members:
have voted for a resolution at a meeting of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee; or
have indicated agreement with a resolution as mentioned in paragraph (2)(a).

section.heading: Disclosure of interests to the Minister

content.p: An Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member must give written notice to the Minister of all interests, pecuniary or otherwise, that the member has or acquires and that conflict or could conflict with the proper performance of the member’s functions.

section.heading: Disclosure of interests to Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee

content.p: An Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member who has an interest, pecuniary or otherwise, in a matter being considered or about to be considered by the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee must disclose the nature of the interest to a meeting of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee.
(2) The disclosure must be made as soon as possible after the relevant facts have come to the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member’s knowledge.
The disclosure must be recorded in the minutes of the meeting of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee.
Unless the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee otherwise determines, the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member:
must not be present during any deliberation by the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee on the matter; and
must not take part in any decision of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee with respect to the matter.
For the purposes of making a determination under subsection (4), the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member:
must not be present during any deliberation of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee for the purpose of making the determination; and
must not take part in making the determination.
A determination under subsection (4) must be recorded in the minutes of the meeting of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee.
The Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee must not engage in paid work outside the duties of the Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee without the Minister’s approval.

An Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member (other than the Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee) must not engage in any paid employment that conflicts or may conflict with the proper performance of his or her duties.

An Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member is to be paid the remuneration that is determined by the Remuneration Tribunal. If no determination of that remuneration by the Tribunal is in operation, the member is to be paid the remuneration that is prescribed.
An Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member is to be paid the allowances that are prescribed.
(3) This section has effect subject to the Remuneration Tribunal Act 1973.
The Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee has the recreation leave entitlements that are determined by the Remuneration Tribunal.

The Minister may grant the Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee leave of absence, other than recreation leave, on the terms and conditions as to remuneration or otherwise that the Minister determines.
The Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee may grant leave of absence to an Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member on the terms and conditions that the Chair determines.
An Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member may resign his or her appointment by giving the Minister a written resignation.
The resignation takes effect on the day it is received by the Minister or, if a later day is specified in the resignation, on that later day.
The Minister may terminate the appointment of an Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member:
for misbehaviour; or
if the member is unable to perform the duties of his or her office because of physical or mental incapacity.
The Minister may terminate the appointment of an Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member if:
the member:
becomes bankrupt; or
takes steps to take the benefit of any law for the relief of bankrupt or insolvent debtors; or
compounds with one or more of his or her creditors; or
makes an assignment of his or her remuneration for the benefit of one or more of his or her creditors; or
the member is absent, except on leave of absence, for 3 consecutive meetings of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee; or
the member fails, without reasonable excuse, to comply with section 261 or 262.
The Minister may terminate the appointment of an Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member if the Minister is of the opinion that the performance of the member has been unsatisfactory.

The Minister may terminate the appointment of the Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee if the Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee engages, except with the Minister’s approval, in paid work outside the duties of the Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee’s office (see subsection 263(1)).

The Minister may terminate the appointment of an Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member (other than the Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee) if the member engages in paid employment that conflicts or may conflict with the proper performance of the member’s duties (see subsection 263(2)).
An Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member holds office on the terms and conditions (if any) in relation to matters not covered by this Act that are determined by the Minister.

section.heading: Assistance to Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee

content.p: Any or all of the following bodies:
the Regulator;
the Department;
any other Department, agency or authority of the Commonwealth;
may assist the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee in the performance of its functions.
The assistance may include the following:
the provision of information;
the provision of advice;
the making available of resources and facilities (including secretariat services and clerical assistance).

If an officer or employee of a body mentioned in subsection (1) assists the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee, the officer or employee is taken, for the purposes of this Act, to be a person assisting the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee under this section.
A person commits an offence if:
the person is, or has been, an entrusted public official; and
the person has obtained protected information in his or her capacity as an entrusted public official; and
the person:
discloses the information to another person; or
uses the information.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years or 120 penalty units, or both.
Exceptions
Each of the following is an exception to the prohibition in subsection (1):
the disclosure or use is authorised by a provision of this Part;
the disclosure or use is in compliance with a requirement under:
a law of the Commonwealth; or
a prescribed law of a State or a Territory.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to a matter in subsection (2) (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
Except where it is necessary to do so for the purposes of giving effect to this Act or a legislative instrument under this Act, an entrusted public official is not to be required:
to produce to a court or tribunal a document containing protected information; or
to disclose protected information to a court or tribunal.
Note: See also the Clean Energy Regulator Act 2011, which deals with the use and disclosure of information by officials of the Clean Energy Regulator.

section.heading: Disclosure or use for the purposes of this Act or a legislative instrument under this Act

content.p: An entrusted public official may disclose or use protected information if:
the disclosure or use is for the purposes of this Act or a legislative instrument under this Act; or
(b) the disclosure or use is for the purposes of the Australian National Registry of Emissions Units Act 2011 or a legislative instrument under that Act;

the disclosure or use is for the purposes of the performance of the functions of the Regulator or the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee under this Act or a legislative instrument under this Act; or
the disclosure or use is in the course of the entrusted public official’s employment or service as an entrusted public official.
An entrusted public official may disclose protected information to the Minister.
An entrusted public official may disclose protected information to:
the Secretary; or
an officer of the Department who is authorised by the Secretary, in writing, for the purposes of this section;
if the disclosure is for the purposes of:
advising the Minister; or
facilitating Australia’s compliance with its international obligations under:
the Climate Change Convention; or
the Kyoto Protocol; or
the Paris Agreement; or
any other international agreement relating to climate change; or
facilitating the development of an international agreement relating to climate change.
An entrusted public official may disclose protected information to a Royal Commission.
The Regulator may, by writing, impose conditions to be complied with in relation to protected audit information disclosed under subsection (1) by:
an audit team leader; or
a person assisting an audit team leader.
The Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee may, by writing, impose conditions to be complied with in relation to protected ERAC information disclosed under subsection (1) by:
the Chair; or
an Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member; or
a person assisting the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee under section 269.
An instrument under subsection (2) or (3) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Disclosure to certain persons and bodies

content.p: Scope
This section applies if the Regulator is satisfied that particular protected audit information will enable or assist any of the following persons or bodies:
Low Carbon Australia Limited (ACN 141 478 748);
the Australian Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre;
a prescribed professional disciplinary body;
a person or body responsible for the administration of a scheme that involves the issue of prescribed eligible carbon units;
to perform or exercise any of the functions or powers of the person or body.
Disclosure
If any of the following individuals:
an individual who is an audit team leader;
an individual assisting an audit team leader;
is authorised by the Regulator, in writing, for the purposes of this section, the individual may disclose that protected audit information to the person or body concerned.
Secondary disclosure and use
A person commits an offence if:
the person is:
a prescribed professional disciplinary body; or
a member of a prescribed professional disciplinary body; and
protected audit information has been disclosed under subsection (3) to the body; and
the person:
discloses the information to another person; or
uses the information.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years or 120 penalty units, or both.
Subsection (4) does not apply if:
the disclosure or use is with the consent of the Regulator; and
the disclosure or use is for the purpose of:
deciding whether or not to take disciplinary or other action; or
taking that action.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to a matter in subsection (5) (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
Conditions
The Regulator may, by writing, impose conditions to be complied with in relation to protected audit information disclosed under subsection (3).
A person commits an offence if:
the person is subject to a condition under subsection (6); and
the person engages in conduct; and
the person’s conduct breaches the condition.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years or 120 penalty units, or both.
An instrument under subsection (6) is not a legislative instrument.
Scope
This section applies if the Regulator is satisfied that particular protected audit information will enable or assist a body corporate that:
either:
conducts, or is involved in the supervision of, a financial market; or
is a body corporate that holds an Australian CS facility licence or an Australian derivative trade repository licence, or that operates a prescribed derivative trade repository; and
is specified in the regulations or the legislative rules;
to monitor compliance with, enforce, or perform functions or exercise powers under:
(c) the Corporations Act 2001; or
the business law of a State or Territory; or
the business law of a foreign country; or
the operating rules (if any) of the body corporate.
Disclosure
If any of the following individuals:
an individual who is an audit team leader;
an individual assisting an audit team leader;
is authorised by the Regulator, in writing, for the purposes of this section, the individual may disclose that protected audit information to the body corporate.
Secondary disclosure and use
A person commits an offence if:
the person is:
a body corporate; or
an officer, employee or agent of a body corporate; and
protected audit information has been disclosed under subsection (3) to the body corporate; and
the person:
discloses the information to another person; or
uses the information.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years or 120 penalty units, or both.
Subsection (4) does not apply if:
the disclosure or use is with the consent of the Regulator; and
the disclosure or use is for the purpose of monitoring compliance with, enforcing, or performing functions or exercising powers under:
(i) the Corporations Act 2001; or
the business law of a State or Territory; or
the business law of a foreign country; or
the operating rules (if any) of the body corporate.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to a matter in subsection (5) (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
Conditions

The Regulator may, by writing, impose conditions to be complied with by the body corporate and its officers, employees and agents in relation to protected audit information disclosed to the body corporate under subsection (3).
A person commits an offence if:
the person is subject to a condition under subsection (6); and
the person engages in conduct; and
the person’s conduct breaches the condition.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years or 120 penalty units, or both.
An instrument under subsection (6) is not a legislative instrument.
Meaning of expressions
(9) In this section, the following expressions have the same meanings as in Chapter 7 of the Corporations Act 2001:
(a) Australian CS facility licence;
(aa) Australian derivative trade repository licence;
(b) financial market;
(c) officer;
(d) operating rules;
(e) prescribed derivative trade repository.
An entrusted public official may disclose protected information that relates to the affairs of a person if:
the person has consented to the disclosure; and
the disclosure is in accordance with that consent.

section.heading: Disclosure to reduce threat to life or health

content.p: An entrusted public official may disclose protected information if:
the entrusted public official believes on reasonable grounds that the disclosure is necessary to prevent or lessen a serious and imminent threat to the life or health of an individual; and
the disclosure is for the purposes of preventing or lessening that threat.
An entrusted public official may disclose protected information if it has already been lawfully made available to the public.
Any of the following persons:
an audit team leader;
a person assisting an audit team leader;
may disclose:
summaries of protected audit information; or
statistics derived from protected audit information;
if those summaries or statistics, as the case may be, are not likely to enable the identification of a person.

section.heading: Disclosure for purposes of law enforcement—protected audit information

content.p: Scope
This section applies if the Regulator is satisfied that disclosure of particular protected audit information is reasonably necessary for:
the enforcement of the criminal law; or
the enforcement of a law imposing a pecuniary penalty; or
the protection of the public revenue.
Disclosure
If any of the following individuals:
an individual who is an audit team leader;
an individual assisting an audit team leader;
is authorised by the Regulator, in writing, for the purposes of this section, the individual may disclose that protected audit information to:
a Department, agency or authority of the Commonwealth, a State or a Territory; or
an Australian police force;
whose functions include that enforcement or protection, for the purposes of that enforcement or protection.
Secondary disclosure and use
A person commits an offence if:
the person is, or has been, an employee or officer of:
a Department, agency or authority of the Commonwealth, a State or a Territory; or
an Australian police force; and
protected audit information has been disclosed under subsection (3) to the Department, agency, authority or police force, as the case may be; and
the person has obtained the information in the person’s capacity as an employee or officer of the Department, agency, authority or police force, as the case may be; and
the person:
discloses the information to another person; or
uses the information.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years or 120 penalty units, or both.
Subsection (4) does not apply if:
the disclosure or use is with the consent of the Regulator; and
the disclosure or use is for the purpose of:
enforcing the criminal law; or
enforcing a law imposing a pecuniary penalty; or
protecting the public revenue.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to a matter in subsection (5) (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
Conditions
The Regulator may, by writing, impose conditions to be complied with in relation to protected audit information disclosed under subsection (3).
A person commits an offence if:
the person is subject to a condition under subsection (6); and
the person engages in conduct; and
the person’s conduct breaches the condition.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years or 120 penalty units, or both.
An instrument under subsection (6) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Disclosure for purposes of law enforcement—protected ERAC information

content.p: Scope
This section applies if the Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee is satisfied that disclosure of particular protected ERAC information is reasonably necessary for:
the enforcement of the criminal law; or
the enforcement of a law imposing a pecuniary penalty; or
the protection of the public revenue.
Disclosure
The Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee may disclose that protected ERAC information to:
a Department, agency or authority of the Commonwealth, a State or a Territory; or
an Australian police force;
whose functions include that enforcement or protection, for the purposes of that enforcement or protection.
If any of the following individuals:
an Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member;
an individual assisting the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee under section 269;
is authorised by the Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee, in writing, for the purposes of this section, the individual may disclose that protected ERAC information to:
a Department, agency or authority of the Commonwealth, a State or a Territory; or
an Australian police force;
whose functions include that enforcement or protection, for the purposes of that enforcement or protection.
Secondary disclosure and use
A person commits an offence if:
the person is, or has been, an employee or officer of:
a Department, agency or authority of the Commonwealth, a State or a Territory; or
an Australian police force; and
protected ERAC information has been disclosed under subsection (2) or (3) to the Department, agency, authority or police force, as the case may be; and
the person has obtained the information in the person’s capacity as an employee or officer of the Department, agency, authority or police force, as the case may be; and
the person:
discloses the information to another person; or
uses the information.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years or 120 penalty units, or both.
Subsection (4) does not apply if:
the disclosure or use is with the consent of the Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee; and
the disclosure or use is for the purpose of:
enforcing the criminal law; or
enforcing a law imposing a pecuniary penalty; or
protecting the public revenue.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to a matter in subsection (5) (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
Conditions
The Chair of the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee may, by writing, impose conditions to be complied with in relation to protected ERAC information disclosed under subsection (2) or (3).
A person commits an offence if:
the person is subject to a condition under subsection (6); and
the person engages in conduct; and
the person’s conduct breaches the condition.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years or 120 penalty units, or both.
An instrument under subsection (6) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Disclosure for purposes of review of Act

content.p: An entrusted public official may disclose protected information to a person if:
the person is conducting a review under section 306; and
the disclosure is for the purposes of that review.
The Regulator has the following functions:
to monitor compliance with this Act and the associated provisions;
to promote compliance with this Act and the associated provisions;
to conduct and/or co-ordinate education programs about this Act and the associated provisions;
to advise the Minister on matters relating to this Act and the associated provisions;
to advise the Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee on matters relating to the making, variation or revocation of methodology determinations;
to advise and assist persons in relation to their obligations under this Act and the associated provisions;
to advise and assist prospective applicants in connection with ensuring that applications are in accordance with this Act;
to advise and assist the representatives of persons in relation to compliance by persons with this Act and the associated provisions;
to liaise with regulatory and other relevant bodies, whether in Australia or elsewhere, about co-operative arrangements for matters relating to this Act and the associated provisions;
to collect, analyse, interpret and disseminate statistical information relating to the operation of this Act and the associated provisions.

The Regulator may, by legislative instrument, arrange for the use, under the Regulator’s control, of computer programs for any purposes for which the Regulator may, or must, under this Act, the regulations or the legislative rules:
make a decision; or
exercise any power or comply with any obligation; or
do anything else related to making a decision or exercising a power or complying with an obligation.
For the purposes of this Act, the regulations and the legislative rules, the Regulator is taken to have:
made a decision; or
exercised a power or complied with an obligation; or
done something else related to the making of a decision or the exercise of a power or the compliance with an obligation;
that was made, exercised, complied with or done by the operation of a computer program under such an arrangement.

section.heading: Regulator’s power to require further information

content.p: Applications
If:
a person makes an application to the Regulator under this Act, the regulations or the legislative rules; and

the Regulator exercises a power, under another provision of this Act, the regulations or the legislative rules, to require the applicant to give the Regulator further information in connection with the application;
the Regulator:
must ensure that the further information is relevant to the matter to which the application relates; and
must ensure that the power is exercised in a reasonable way.
Requests
If:
a person makes a request to the Regulator under this Act; and
the Regulator exercises a power, under another provision of this Act, to require the person to give the Regulator further information in connection with the request;
the Regulator:
must ensure that the further information is relevant to the matter to which the request relates; and
must ensure that the power is exercised in a reasonable way.

section.heading: Information previously given to the Regulator

content.p: If:
on a particular occasion, a person gave information to the Regulator under this Act, the regulations or the legislative rules; and
the person is subsequently required or permitted, under this Act, the regulations or the legislative rules, to give the same information to the Regulator;
the person is taken to have given the information to the Regulator on that later occasion.

section.heading: Actions may be taken by an agent of a project proponent

content.p: The principles of agency apply in relation to the taking, by a project proponent for an eligible offsets project, of any of the following actions under this Act, the regulations or the legislative rules:
making an application;
giving information in connection with an application;
withdrawing an application;
giving a report;
giving a notice (including an electronic notice);
making a submission;
making a request;
giving information in connection with a request.

For example, the project proponent may authorise another person to be the project proponent’s agent for the purposes of making an application under this Act, the regulations or the legislative rules on the project proponent’s behalf.
To avoid doubt, this section does not, by implication, limit the application of the principles of agency to other matters arising under this Act, the regulations or the legislative rules.
The Minister may, by writing, delegate any or all of his or her functions or powers under this Act, the regulations or the legislative rules to:
the Secretary; or
an SES employee, or acting SES employee, in the Department.
Note: The expressions SES employee and acting SES employee are defined in the Acts Interpretation Act 1901.
In exercising powers under a delegation, the delegate must comply with any directions of the Minister.
Subsection (1) does not apply to a power to make, vary or revoke a legislative instrument, unless the power is conferred by:
subsection 106(1) (power to make a methodology determination); or
subsection 114(1) (power to vary a methodology determination); or
subparagraph 122(1)(b)(ii) (power to specify the duration of a methodology determination); or
subsection 123(1) (power to revoke a methodology determination).

section.heading: Delegation by a State Minister or a Territory Minister

content.p: A Minister of a State or Territory may, by writing, delegate any or all of his or her functions or powers under this Act to a person who:
is an officer or employee of the State or Territory, as the case may be; and
holds or performs the duties of an office or position that is equivalent to a position occupied by an SES employee in the Australian Public Service.
In exercising powers under a delegation, the delegate must comply with any directions of the Minister of the State or the Minister of the Territory, as the case may be.

The Secretary may, by writing, delegate any or all of his or her functions or powers under this Act, the regulations or the legislative rules to an SES employee, or acting SES employee, in the Department.
Note: The expressions SES employee and acting SES employee are defined in the Acts Interpretation Act 1901.
In exercising powers under a delegation, the delegate must comply with any directions of the Secretary.

section.heading: Concurrent operation of State and Territory laws

content.p: This Act is not intended to exclude or limit the operation of a law of a State or Territory that is capable of operating concurrently with this Act.

section.heading: Law relating to legal professional privilege not affected

content.p: This Act does not affect the law relating to legal professional privilege.
States
The Minister may make arrangements with a Minister of a State with respect to the administration of this Act, including:
arrangements for the performance of the functions of a magistrate under this Act by a magistrate of that State; and
(b) arrangements for the exercise of the powers conferred by section 39 on relevant land registration officials of that State; and

The Minister may arrange with a Minister of a State with whom an arrangement is in force under subsection (1) for the variation or revocation of the arrangement.
Australian Capital Territory

arrangements for the performance of the functions of a magistrate under this Act by a magistrate of the Australian Capital Territory; and
(b) arrangements for the exercise of the powers conferred by section 39 on relevant land registration officials of the Australian Capital Territory; and
(c) arrangements for the exercise of the powers conferred by section 40 on relevant land registration officials of the Australian Capital Territory.
The Minister may arrange with a Minister of the Australian Capital Territory for the variation or revocation of an arrangement in force under subsection (3).
Northern Territory

arrangements for the performance of the functions of a magistrate under this Act by a magistrate of the Northern Territory; and
(b) arrangements for the exercise of the powers conferred by section 39 on relevant land registration officials of the Northern Territory; and
(c) arrangements for the exercise of the powers conferred by section 40 on relevant land registration officials of the Northern Territory.

Gazettal

None of the following:
the Minister;
a delegate of the Minister;
the Secretary;
a delegate of the Secretary;
the Regulator;
a delegate of the Regulator;
an inspector;
a person assisting an inspector;
an audit team leader;
an Emissions Reduction Assurance Committee member;
is liable to an action or other proceeding for damages for, or in relation to, an act or matter in good faith done or omitted to be done:
in the performance or purported performance of any function; or
in the exercise or purported exercise of any power;
conferred by this Act (other than section 20D or 20E) or the associated provisions.
This Act does not, by implication, limit the executive power of the Commonwealth.
The purpose of this section is to ensure that amounts payable under this Act, the regulations or the legislative rules are notionally payable by the Commonwealth (or parts of the Commonwealth).

(2) The Minister responsible for administering the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013 may give written directions for the purposes of this section, including directions relating to the transfer of amounts within, or between, accounts operated by the Commonwealth.

If the operation of this Act, the regulations or the legislative rules would result in an acquisition of property from a person otherwise than on just terms, the Commonwealth is liable to pay a reasonable amount of compensation to the person.

acquisition of property has the same meaning as in paragraph 51(xxxi) of the Constitution.
just terms has the same meaning as in paragraph 51(xxxi) of the Constitution.
This Act does not affect the operation of the Native Title Act 1993.
This Act does not affect the operation of the Racial Discrimination Act 1975.
Without limiting its effect apart from this section, this Act and the associated provisions also have effect as provided by this section.
External affairs
This Act and the associated provisions also have the effect they would have if:
subsections (3) and (4) had not been enacted; and
this Act and the associated provisions did not apply except to the extent to which they relate to:
matters of international concern; or
matters external to Australia.
Limited types of offsets projects

This Act and the associated provisions also have the effect they would have if subsection (2) had not been enacted and each reference in this Act and the associated provisions to an offsets project were, by express provision, confined to an offsets project:
where the project proponent is, or each of the project proponents are, a constitutional corporation; or
where the project proponent is:
the Commonwealth; or
an authority of the Commonwealth; or
that is, or is to be, carried on in a Territory; or
that is, or is to be, carried on in a Commonwealth place; or
that is, or is to be, carried on in the course of, or in relation to, any of the following:
trade or commerce between Australia and places outside Australia;
trade or commerce among the States;
trade or commerce within a Territory, between a State or Territory or between 2 Territories.
Limited power to purchase prescribed eligible carbon units
This Act and the associated provisions also have the effect they would have if:
subsection (2) had not been enacted; and

this Act, by express provision, prohibited the Regulator from entering into a carbon abatement contract, on behalf of the Commonwealth, for the purchase by the Commonwealth of prescribed eligible carbon units unless the units represent carbon abatement by a constitutional corporation.

section.heading: Prescribing matters by reference to other instruments

content.p: The regulations or the legislative rules may make provision in relation to a matter by applying, adopting or incorporating, with or without modification, a matter contained in an instrument or writing:
as in force or existing at a particular time; or
as in force or existing from time to time.
(2) Subsection (1) has effect despite anything in subsection 14(2) of the Legislation Act 2003.

If the regulations or the legislative rules make provision in relation to a matter by applying, adopting or incorporating, with or without modification, a matter contained in an instrument or writing, the Regulator must ensure that the text of the matter applied, adopted or incorporated is published on the Regulator’s website.
Subsection (3) does not apply if the publication would infringe copyright.
The regulations may make provision in relation to a matter by conferring a power to make a decision of an administrative character on the Regulator.

section.heading: Administrative decisions under the legislative rules

content.p: The legislative rules may make provision in relation to a matter by conferring a power to make a decision of an administrative character on the Regulator.

section.heading: Periodic reviews of operation of this Act etc.

content.p: The Climate Change Authority must conduct reviews of the operation of:
this Act; and
the regulations; and
other instruments made under this Act.
Public consultation
A review under subsection (1) must make provision for public consultation.
Report
The Climate Change Authority must:
give the Minister a report of the review; and
as soon as practicable after giving the report to the Minister, publish the report on the Climate Change Authority’s website.
The Minister must cause copies of a report under subsection (3) to be tabled in each House of the Parliament within 15 sitting days of that House after the review is completed.
First review
The first review under subsection (1) must be completed before the end of 31 December 2014.
Subsequent reviews
Each subsequent review under subsection (1) must be completed within 3 years after the deadline for completion of the previous review.
For the purposes of subsections (4), (5) and (6), a review is completed when the report of the review is given to the Minister under subsection (3).
Recommendations
A report of a review under subsection (1) may set out recommendations to the Commonwealth Government.
In formulating a recommendation that the Commonwealth Government should take particular action, the Climate Change Authority must analyse the costs and benefits of that action.
Subsection (9) does not prevent the Climate Change Authority from taking other matters into account in formulating a recommendation.

If a report of a review under subsection (1) sets out one or more recommendations to the Commonwealth Government, the report must set out the Climate Change Authority’s reasons for those recommendations.
Government response to recommendations
If a report of a review under subsection (1) sets out one or more recommendations to the Commonwealth Government:
as soon as practicable after receiving the report, the Minister must cause to be prepared a statement setting out the Commonwealth Government’s response to each of the recommendations; and
within 6 months after receiving the report, the Minister must cause copies of the statement to be tabled in each House of the Parliament.
The Commonwealth Government’s response to the recommendations may have regard to the views of the following:
the Climate Change Authority;
the Clean Energy Regulator;
such other persons as the Minister considers relevant.
The Governor-General may make regulations prescribing matters:
required or permitted by this Act to be prescribed; or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Act.
The Minister may, by legislative instrument, make rules (legislative rules) prescribing matters:
(a) required or permitted by this Act to be prescribed by the legislative rules; or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Act.

If, despite the misdescription, the amendment can be given effect as intended, then the misdescribed amendment can be incorporated through an editorial change made under section 15V of the Legislation Act 2003.
